q: How much does a residential solar system cost per kW?
a: Residential rooftop solar from Helios Solar costs between Rs 65,000 and Rs 75,000 per kW installed, before subsidy. The exact figure depends on panel type, roof structure and inverter choice.

q: What does a 3 kW rooftop system cost?
a: A 3 kW residential system runs about Rs 1.95 lakh to Rs 2.25 lakh before subsidy. It typically generates 360 to 400 units a month in our service areas.

q: What does a 5 kW rooftop system cost?
a: A 5 kW residential system runs about Rs 3.25 lakh to Rs 3.75 lakh before subsidy, and generates roughly 600 to 650 units a month.

q: What does a 10 kW system cost?
a: A 10 kW system costs about Rs 6.5 lakh to Rs 7.5 lakh before subsidy. Above 10 kW we usually quote as a commercial installation.

q: Is there a government subsidy for rooftop solar?
a: Yes. Under the national rooftop solar scheme, residential customers can claim a central subsidy of Rs 30,000 per kW for the first 2 kW and Rs 18,000 per kW for the third kW, capped at Rs 78,000 per household. Helios Solar files the application for you.

q: Do commercial installations get a subsidy?
a: No. The residential rooftop subsidy does not apply to commercial or industrial connections. Commercial customers usually benefit instead from accelerated depreciation on the asset.

q: How long does the subsidy take to arrive?
a: The subsidy is credited directly to your bank account, typically 30 to 45 days after installation is complete and the distribution company has inspected and commissioned the system.

q: What is the warranty on the solar panels?
a: Panels carry a 25 year performance warranty and a 12 year product warranty. The performance warranty guarantees at least 80 percent of rated output at year 25.

q: What is the warranty on the inverter?
a: Inverters carry a 10 year warranty. Extended cover to 15 years is available for about 4 percent of system cost.

q: What warranty covers the mounting structure?
a: The galvanised mounting structure carries a 15 year warranty against rust and structural failure, and is rated for wind speeds up to 150 km/h.

q: Does Helios Solar warranty the installation work itself?
a: Yes. Workmanship, cabling and waterproofing carry a 5 year warranty. Any leak or wiring fault traced to our installation is repaired free.

q: How long does installation take?
a: Installation takes 2 to 3 weeks from the site visit. That covers structural survey, material delivery, mounting, wiring and commissioning.

q: How long does the whole process take end to end?
a: From first enquiry to a working system is usually 5 to 7 weeks: about a week to schedule and complete the site visit, 2 to 3 weeks for installation, and 2 to 3 weeks for net metering approval and commissioning.

q: How long does the physical installation on my roof take?
a: The work on your roof takes 2 to 3 days for a typical residential system. Larger commercial installations take 1 to 2 weeks.

q: What happens during a site visit?
a: An engineer measures your usable roof area, checks the shadow profile through the day, inspects the roof structure and your existing electrical panel, and reads your last twelve months of bills. The visit takes about an hour and is free.

q: Is the site visit free?
a: Yes, the site visit and the quotation that follows are completely free with no obligation to buy.

q: What is net metering?
a: Net metering lets you export surplus solar power to the grid and receive credit for it. Your bill is calculated on net consumption, which is what you drew from the grid minus what you sent back.

q: How do I apply for net metering?
a: Helios Solar files the net metering application with your distribution company on your behalf. Approval and meter installation normally take 2 to 3 weeks after commissioning.

q: What happens to the extra power I generate?
a: Surplus units are exported to the grid and credited against future consumption. Credits carry forward through the billing year, and unused credit is settled at the end of the year at the rate your distribution company sets.

q: Will solar work during a power cut?
a: A standard grid-tied system shuts down during an outage for the safety of line workers. To keep power during a cut you need a hybrid inverter with battery storage, which we can quote separately.

q: Do I need a battery?
a: Most customers do not. Batteries add roughly Rs 45,000 to Rs 60,000 per kWh of storage and are worth it mainly where outages are frequent or the grid connection is unreliable.

q: How much maintenance does a solar system need?
a: Very little. Panels need washing with plain water every 4 to 6 weeks in dusty months, and an electrical inspection once a year. There are no moving parts.

q: Do you offer an annual maintenance contract?
a: Yes. Our annual maintenance contract costs Rs 4,500 per year for systems up to 5 kW and covers four cleaning visits, an annual electrical check and priority fault response within 48 hours.

q: What happens if a panel stops working?
a: Call us and we will inspect within 48 hours. A panel failing inside its 12 year product warranty is replaced free, including labour.

q: Which areas does Helios Solar serve?
a: We install in Hyderabad, Warangal, Vijayawada and Bengaluru, along with the surrounding districts of each.

q: Do you install outside your service areas?
a: For commercial projects above 50 kW we travel anywhere in Telangana, Andhra Pradesh and Karnataka. Residential installations are limited to Hyderabad, Warangal, Vijayawada and Bengaluru.

q: Do you offer financing or EMI?
a: Yes. We partner with lenders offering solar loans from 7.5 percent annual interest over 3 to 7 years, typically with no down payment for residential systems up to 10 kW.

q: Can I pay in instalments directly to Helios?
a: We take 30 percent on order, 50 percent on material delivery and 20 percent on commissioning. Anything longer than that goes through one of our loan partners.

q: How much will I save on my electricity bill?
a: A well sized system typically covers 70 to 90 percent of a household's consumption. Most of our residential customers cut their monthly bill from around Rs 3,500 to under Rs 700.

q: How long until the system pays for itself?
a: After subsidy, most residential systems pay back in 3.5 to 4.5 years. Commercial systems with accelerated depreciation usually pay back in 3 to 4 years.

q: How long do solar panels last?
a: Panels last 25 to 30 years. Output declines by roughly half a percent a year, so a panel still produces around 85 percent of its original output after 25 years.

q: How much roof area do I need?
a: Allow about 100 square feet of shadow free roof per kW. A 5 kW system therefore needs roughly 500 square feet.

q: Will solar work on my roof if it is shaded?
a: Partial shade reduces output. Where shade is unavoidable we fit power optimisers or microinverters so one shaded panel does not drag down the rest of the string, which adds about 8 to 12 percent to system cost.

q: Can you install on a sloped or tiled roof?
a: Yes. We install on flat concrete, sloped tile and metal sheet roofs. Tiled roofs need specific hooks that add a small amount to the structure cost.

q: Will the panels damage or leak through my roof?
a: No. On concrete roofs we use ballasted or chemically anchored mounts and seal every penetration. Waterproofing is covered by our 5 year workmanship warranty.

q: What brand of panels do you use?
a: We fit tier one monocrystalline panels, usually 545 W to 585 W modules. The exact make depends on availability at the time of order and is named in your written quotation.

q: Do you use Indian made panels?
a: Yes, we default to domestically manufactured modules from the approved list, which is also a requirement for claiming the residential subsidy.

q: What documents do I need to go solar?
a: You need a recent electricity bill, proof of identity, proof of ownership or a no objection letter from the owner, and a passport photograph. We handle the rest of the paperwork.

q: Can I go solar if I rent my home?
a: Yes, with a written no objection certificate from the property owner. The subsidy is claimed against the electricity connection holder.

q: What size system should I choose?
a: Size it against your consumption. Roughly, every 1 kW generates 120 to 130 units a month in our service areas, so divide your average monthly units by 125 to get an approximate system size in kW.

q: Do you remove the panels if I sell my house?
a: The system stays with the property and transfers to the new owner. We update the warranty and net metering records to the new owner's name at no charge.

q: How do I get a quotation?
a: Book a free site visit. You get a written quotation within two working days of the visit, itemising panels, inverter, structure, cabling, installation, the expected subsidy and the projected monthly saving.
